text:
maya: Nightly perf alert triggered for eu-gpu-small pool — throughput down ~11%, P95 latency jumped from ~120ms to ~220ms after r3542 deploy. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/nightly/runner-eu-gpu-small :eyes:
arjun: ugh, saw the alert. Any obvious changelog in r3542?
maya: r3542 merged PR #987 — batch-scheduler change: 'prefer-fill' window tweak and small KV prefetch hint adjustments.
lin: quick look at profiler flamegraph for a hot host: https://prof.redwood.ai/fg/3914820000 — kernel runtime spikes around token gen step. KV miss rate also spikes (~0.6 -> 5.2%).
elena: perf-ci shows a regression on perf-ci-merge-3542 job: https://ci.redwood.ai/job/perf-ci-merge-3542 — job 12 failed P99 and throughput tests.
perf-ci: [bot] perf job ended: FAIL. Metric delta: throughput -10.8%, p95 +97ms, kv_miss_rate +4.6%
arjun: can we bisect between r3539..r3542 quickly? I suspect the batching window change triggered different batching boundaries and caused more cold KV accesses + slower kernel fallback.
lin: I ran a quick local repro with a synthetic trace — command: ```python tools/repro/run_load.py --model gpt-slim --seq 1024 --concurrency 32 --batch-policy prefer-fill``` Observed same latency tail.
maya: good repro. Logs show: ```kernel_selector: selected kernel=streamed_attention_slow fallback=true reason=kv_cache_miss_threshold```
arjun: so kernel_selector fell back to slower implementation when KV miss rate > 3% per batch. That matches the KV miss spike. Why did miss rate increase though?
lin: batching heuristic moved some short+long requests into the same batch, increasing avg seq length variance -> poorer KV cache locality -> more evictions.
elena: can we hotfix by reverting batching heuristic until we root cause? That would unblock the rollout.
maya: deploy-bot, what is the canary footprint for r3542?
deploy-bot: [bot] r3542 is in 8% canary on eu-gpu-small (hosts h/eu-03..h/eu-10). No rollbacks scheduled.
arjun: request: run a narrow revert (PR #987 revert) on canary first and watch nightly. If perf improves, proceed to full revert.
lin: started bisect script: `scripts/perf_bisect.sh --range r3539..r3542 --hosts eu-gpu-small --metric throughput` — kicking off now.
perf-ci: [bot] bisect run created: /bisects/3914820000-setup — will post updates.
maya: meanwhile plan: 1) revert #987 in canary 2) add a sampling probe to batcher to measure seq-length variance in real traffic 3) add telemetry to kernel_selector to record miss-rate triggers
elena: agree. I'll open revert PR and a follow-up telemetry PR.
arjun: small mitigation we can try without revert: lower kernel_selector KV miss threshold from 3% -> 8% for canary only. That avoids premature fallbacks. Risks: can increase rare black-swan slowdowns if true misses.
lin: I'll run a quick canary with threshold change on 2 hosts and report.
maya: update after 20m: canary revert applied to eu-04, eu-05. Early numbers: throughput +4.5% on those hosts, p95 down ~35ms. Still need full bisect to be sure.
lin: threshold change trial: hosts eu-06, eu-07 show reduced fallbacks but KV miss latency still slightly higher.
arjun: conclusion so far: batching change increased cross-request seq variance -> more KV churn -> kernel_selector frequently choosing fallback slow kernel. Root cause is batching heuristic interacting with cache eviction thresholds.
elena: action items: (1) full revert PR to unblock rollout (2) follow-up: change batching to be size-aware (3) add kernel_selector telemetry and sampling (4) tighten CI perf tests to synthesize mixed seq workloads.
maya: +1. I'll monitor overnight. Reopen thread if anything spikes. :white_check_mark:
